speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has presented unprecedented challenges in our employment landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will help workers and companies tackle the immediate challenges to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Before COVID-19, we had been preparing workers and employers for the future of work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These efforts must now shift to even higher gear.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will deepen and expand efforts to ensure fairness at work, with a focus on giving every worker a chance to be meaningfully employed, and fostering an inclusive workforce and progressive workplaces.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our economic agencies will press on with industry transformation to keep as many Singaporeans as possible in jobs, and create new jobs to make up for job losses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Workforce Singapore and its partners will strive to open up pathways for every newly displaced worker to return to meaningful employment: (a) We will work with employers to make jobs available to jobseekers willing to acquire new skills, through heavily subsidised training and the Jobs Growth Incentive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Where employers remain cautious about hiring, we will support them to host traineeships and attachments, by co-funding the training allowance with host organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will allow jobseekers to gain industry-relevant skills and be better positioned for economic recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will give stronger support to employers that favourably consider middle-aged and mature workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (b) We will intensify efforts to help Singaporeans in their job search.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will expand our offerings and improve accessibility through: (i) SGUnited Jobs & Skills Centres across all HDB towns; (ii) Enhanced Digital Career Matching Services; (iii) Private sector employment agencies serving as SGUnited Jobs & Skills Placement Partners.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singaporeans, regardless of age, race, gender, must have a fair chance at job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While employment rates have risen for mature workers, women and ethnic minorities, we must remain vigilant and build on the gains.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our foreign workforce policies have been designed to support economic growth, so as to create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is regular calibration, to enable firms to access the manpower they need while ensuring a strong Singaporean core.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the last decade, we have also made policy adjustments to spur businesses to upgrade productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through expanded opportunities, nearly six in 10 locals in the workforce today are employed in Professional, Managerial, Executive and Technician (PMET) jobs, among the highest in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For every Employment Pass (EP) holder, there are nearly seven locals employed in PMET roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as we stay open to the world to accelerate our recovery, the crisis makes it all the more important that employers give fair treatment to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They should also seek to achieve greater diversity within their EP and S Pass workforce where practical.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will ensure that employers uphold both the letter and spirit of the Fair Consideration Framework.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will closely examine retrenchment exercises to ensure they are carried out fairly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses that bring in skills in short supply or new networks of opportunity for Singapore will always remain welcome.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, we will require businesses to invest more effort to develop and strengthen their Singaporean core.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: COVID-19 has accentuated the fast-changing nature of employment, and the uncertainty for those who are self-employed to find consistent work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This affects their income stability and ability to save regularly for retirement and healthcare needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to implement the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Self-Employed Persons (SEPs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have piloted the contribute-as-you-earn model earlier this year to help SEPs make small and regular Medisave contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We aim to reduce payment-related disputes, mitigate the loss of income due to prolonged illness or injury, and support SEPs in their skills needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will further review the responsibilities of service-buyers and intermediaries to bring about a fairer and more balanced relationship with their self-employed workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Uplifting wages at the lower end remains a key priority.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When enhancements to Workfare are included, the gains are even larger.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the context of the current downturn and very uncertain outlook for the economy, our overriding objective is to ensure continued employment opportunities for these workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This effort to raise wages at the lower end will require long-term commitment and new mindsets among employers, service buyers, and society at large.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We may have to pay slightly more for services, so that lower income workers are able to take on better jobs and earn higher wages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Together with the Government's support for lower income workers through Workfare and other schemes, it will help us mitigate inequalities and strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will undertake regular reviews of Workfare and Silver Support.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is also an additional wage offset when employers hire PwDs who have not been working for at least six months.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to look out for gaps in our social safety nets, and enhance support in sustainable ways, and ensure every Singaporean who makes the effort gets a fair chance to bounce back from employment setbacks.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: COVID-19 has led to individuals facing considerable stress.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will need a renewed focus on the health and wellness of the entire workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will forge partnerships with Trade Associations & Chambers, Non-Governmental Organisations and professional bodies, to broaden and strengthen the network of support for our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the last five months, the Task Force has provided assurance to migrant workers at the dormitories and cleared the dormitories of COVID-19 infection.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The new ACE Group will ensure dormitories and other migrant worker housing are safe and resilient against public health threats, by building a stronger system of medical support for migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will also partner with the community and migrant worker groups to meet the social needs of workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As important as it is to safeguard the health and wellness of our workers, we must also ensure the higher costs are sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, we will carefully consider the cost-sharing model for higher standards in migrant worker dormitories and develop an insurance programme to help employers manage unexpectedly large medical expenses of their migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The "new normal" brought about by COVID-19 provides a great opportunity to review workplace practices and entrench more flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will serve public health objectives, and improve business continuity and work-life harmony (WLH).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will implement the Citizens' Panel’s recommendations to support employers to offer FWAs and WLH initiatives and promote greater awareness through diagnostic tools, ambassadors, and recognising progressive employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our tripartite partners are jointly committed to working closely with Singaporeans to overcome the economic and labour market challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help our workers and business succeed, we will continue to uphold fair opportunities, fair hiring, fair competition, and fair support for everyone to progress at every stage of their working lives.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In collaboration with the whole-of-society as part of the SG Together movement, we can and will emerge stronger from this crisis as a cohesive society.
